summary: Hard if your agent reads or changes email: Google requires a restricted-scope review plus a paid security audit (CASA) every year. If your agent only sends email, you skip the audit.
cost: $500–4,500/year security audit if you read or change mail; otherwise free

requirements.text: A Google account and a Google Cloud project (free)
A domain you own, with a public home page and a privacy policy on it
A privacy policy that follows Google's User Data Policy, including the Limited Use rules
Budget for a CASA security assessment if your agent reads or changes mail

steps.text: Create a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: console.cloud.google.com → APIs & Services → Library → Gmail API → Enable

steps.text: Pick the narrowest Gmail scopes your agent needs
steps.detail: Send only → gmail.send (no audit). Read, label or archive mail → gmail.readonly or gmail.modify (restricted: review + audit).

steps.text: Draft the privacy policy and the explanation of why you need each scope
Set up the OAuth consent screen: app name, logo, support email, home page, privacy policy, authorized domain
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform → Branding. Choose Audience: External.

steps.text: Create an OAuth client and add your redirect URI
steps.detail: Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID → Web application. The redirect URI must match exactly what your app sends.

steps.text: Add test users and connect your own account
steps.detail: Up to 100 test users. In Testing, logins expire after 7 days.

steps.text: Verify your domain in Google Search Console
steps.detail: Use a Google account that is Owner or Editor on the Cloud project.

steps.text: Record a demo video of the consent screen and each scope in use
steps.detail: The agent can write the script and shot list; you record it.
Brand verification first, then scope verification.

steps.text: Complete the CASA security assessment with a Google-approved assessor
steps.detail: Only for restricted scopes. Repeat at least every 12 months.
Google says it "can potentially take several weeks".
Removes the 100-user cap and the 7-day login expiry.

blockers.problem: Review rejected: privacy policy doesn't follow Google's Limited Use rules
blockers.fix: Say exactly how Gmail data is used and stored, and that it isn't sold, used for ads, or read by people except as allowed. Resubmit.

blockers.problem: Review rejected: demo video doesn't show every scope
blockers.fix: Re-record it showing the consent screen and each requested scope in action.

blockers.problem: Users see "Google hasn't verified this app", or you hit 100 users
blockers.fix: Expected until verification is done. Add people as test users in the meantime.

blockers.problem: Users get logged out every 7 days during testing
blockers.fix: A Testing-mode limit. It goes away once the app is published.

blockers.problem: Review drags on because you asked for more access than you use
blockers.fix: Drop scopes you don't use. If you only send email, use gmail.send alone.

couldNotVerify: How long restricted-scope review actually takes. Google only says "several weeks" and publishes no deadline.
Current CASA prices. Only third-party sources give figures, so get quotes from approved assessors.
How Google reports a wrong redirect URI. Testing it needs a real OAuth client.

claims.statement: Gmail scopes that read or change mail (for example gmail.readonly and gmail.modify) are restricted scopes.
Restricted scopes need restricted-scope verification, which "can potentially take several weeks to complete."
Apps that access restricted data from or through a third-party server need a security assessment (CASA) by a Google-approved assessor, repeated at least every 12 months.
claims.note: Page says: "complete a security assessment at least every 12 months".

claims.statement: A CASA assessment costs roughly $500–4,500 depending on the assessor and assurance level. Google itself charges nothing.
claims.note: Third-party figure. Google doesn't publish prices; assessors quote individually.

claims.statement: gmail.send on its own is a sensitive scope, not restricted: it needs verification but no CASA assessment.
claims.note: The scopes page classes gmail.send as sensitive; the CASA requirement applies to restricted scopes.

claims.statement: An app in Testing is limited to 100 test users, and their logins (including refresh tokens) expire after 7 days.

sources.title: Google Cloud Help: Manage app audience

claims.note: Page says: "limited to up to 100 test users".

claims.statement: Brand verification typically takes 2–3 business days and comes before scope verification.
claims.note: Only needed if branding changed since the last approved verification.

claims.statement: Verification requires verified domain ownership in Search Console, a public home page, and a privacy policy that complies with the Google API Services User Data Policy.
The submission needs a demo video showing the consent flow and how each sensitive or restricted scope is used.
Unverified apps show an "unverified app" screen and are limited to 100 new users until verified.
Google's authorize endpoint is live and rejects an unknown client ID with "invalid_client: The OAuth client was not found."

sources.title: Probe: authorize endpoint with a fake client ID

claims.statement: 6–10 weeks to production with restricted scopes, and 1–2 days of hands-on work.
claims.note: Our estimate: 2–3 days brand review + several weeks scope review + the CASA assessment. Google publishes no deadline.
